findings.evidence: `pkg/types/time.go:454`..`pkg/types/time.go:471`: on `ErrTimestampInDSTTransition`, `Time.Convert` appends a warning then returns `Time{FromGoTime(tAdj)}` (`pkg/types/time.go:468`). `FromGoTime`/`FromDate` (`pkg/types/time.go:182`..`pkg/types/time.go:204`) build a `CoreTime` with the low 4 `fspTt` bits clear (bit layout shows `fspTtBitFieldOffset=0` and `microsecondBitFieldOffset=4` at `pkg/types/time.go:233`..`pkg/types/time.go:265`). `Time.Type()` treats LSB==0 as `mysql.TypeDatetime` (`pkg/types/time.go:295`..`pkg/types/time.go:304`), so the returned value is DATETIME (fsp=0) rather than TIMESTAMP. Downstream encoding/flattening uses `t.Type()` to decide whether to convert timestamps to/from UTC when the explicit `tp` is unavailable (`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:194`..`pkg/util/codec/codec.go:205`, `pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go:400`..`pkg/tablecodec/tablecodec.go:413`). Executor expression CAST time→time relies on `res.Convert(...)` without re-setting type except for DATE (`pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go:1831`..`pkg/expression/builtin_cast.go:1847`).
findings.fix: In `Time.Convert`, preserve `t1`’s `fspTt` bits when applying the adjustment: e.g. `t1.SetCoreTime(FromGoTime(tAdj)); ctx.AppendWarning(err); return t1, nil`. Alternatively `return NewTime(FromGoTime(tAdj), mysql.TypeTimestamp, t1.Fsp()), nil` (but ensure `fsp` is preserved as intended).
findings.impact: DST-gap conversions to TIMESTAMP can silently return a DATETIME-typed `types.Time`. Any later path that infers timestamp-ness from `t.Type()` (encoding/index keys, row flattening, or executor functions branching on time type) may skip TIMESTAMP-specific timezone handling, risking incorrect key/value encoding (missing loc→UTC conversion) and wrong SQL/runtime semantics around DST transitions.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `upstream/master:pkg/types/time.go` still contains `return Time{FromGoTime(tAdj)}, nil` (no fix after this commit).
findings.verify: Add a focused unit test for `types.Time.Convert` in a DST-skip zone (e.g. `Europe/Amsterdam`) asserting that converting an invalid-gap DATETIME to TIMESTAMP returns `TypeTimestamp` (not DATETIME) and preserves/sets expected fsp. Also add an executor-level SQL test like `SELECT CAST(CAST('2025-03-30 02:30:00' AS DATETIME) AS TIMESTAMP)` and ensure downstream encoding/index-range behavior matches expected UTC conversion (and warnings).
findings.what: `types.Time.Convert` DST-adjustment returns `Time{FromGoTime(...)}`, which drops the TIMESTAMP type/fsp bits; the adjusted result becomes a DATETIME-typed `types.Time` even though the target type is TIMESTAMP.

subject: types/time: invalid timestamp during DST spring forward fixed to next valid ts instead of zero date. (#61533)
